subject: Post-demo recap: multi-region performance & hyperscaler comparison — proposed next tests
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@edgebox.io>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: multi-region performance & hyperscaler comparison — proposed next tests

Hi Aisha / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context on Acme's latency and residency constraints for the European storefronts. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary from today's demo:
- Redwood key differentiators you highlighted as important: predictable p99 latency under load, regional routing/data residency options, and cost controls (batching + cache).
- You are running a pilot with a vector search + generation flow that will be sensitive to sub-200ms token latency for EU customers during peak traffic.
- Acme is currently evaluating: AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex AI Matching, and Redwood hosted/dedicated proposals.

Competitive checklist (what you asked us to compare explicitly):
1) Multi-region p50/p95/p99 latency for the same model family (open Llama-derivative) across US/EU/APAC.
2) Regional availability & data residency guarantees (EU-hosted endpoints, audit logs, KMS support).
3) Cost per 1k tokens at baseline and with batching/caching optimizations.
4) Failure/fallback behavior & SLA commitments.

Proposed next tests (what we'd like permission to run and what we need from you):
- Short latency run: synthetic traffic from eu-west-1, us-east-1, ap-southeast-1 to compare Redwood Hosted (eu endpoint) vs Bedrock vs Vertex for the same model. Expected duration: 2 hours.
- Production-like throughput test: 10min ramp to 100 concurrent sessions hitting the generation + KV cache warm path (to measure p99 tail under batching). Expected duration: 30–60 minutes.
- Residency verification: provide a sample payload and an addressable EU storage bucket so we can demonstrate that logs/artefacts never leave EU when routed to the EU control plane (requires short-term access).

What we will deliver after tests:
- A short matrix (attached) with p50/p95/p99, cost estimates, and recommended deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) per region.
- Specific configuration suggestions (batch size, cache TTL, quantization profile) to meet your latency budget.

Attachments included here: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx (baseline comparators), SLA-and-data-residency-note.pdf (summary of our EU controls).

Ask: can you confirm A) which EU region you want us to target for the residency test (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1), and B) whether we can schedule the latency run early next week (Mon/Tue preferred)?

Thanks — I'll coordinate internal bench work and loop in Vivek/Aditya for the test plan.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

[Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 95KB)]
[Attachment: SLA-and-data-residency-note.pdf (pdf, 62KB)]

From: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@acme-retail.com>

Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: multi-region performance & hyperscaler comparison — proposed next tests

Hi Camila — thanks for the clear recap.

We'd like to proceed with the tests. Quick answers: 
- EU region: please use eu-west-1 as the residency/latency target (this aligns with our current storefronts).
- Time: Mon Jun 8 morning PT (or Tue Jun 9 morning PT) works for the team — prefer Mon if you can.

Two asks from our security/compliance side before we run any payloads: 
1) A short note confirming encryption-at-rest keys for EU endpoints (KMS/HSM) — your SLA doc was helpful but the compliance team wants the exact key locations.
2) An estimated cost delta vs Bedrock for sustained 100k tokens/day after batching recommendations (ballpark is fine).

Tom: looping you to confirm whether EdgeBox (our infra partner) will provide the EU test agent IP ranges or whether Redwood should generate the traffic from Redwood's test agents.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Gupta
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Retail
Aisha.Gupta@acme-retail.com

[Note: I redacted internal PII from the example payloads; we'll share a small sample when you confirm EU KMS details.]

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@acme-retail.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@edgebox.io>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Post-demo recap: multi-region performance & hyperscaler comparison — proposed next tests

Hi Vivek / Aditya — forwarding Acme's confirmation. Two urgent items for the bench:

1) Latency run (Mon Jun 8 AM PT) — we need a reproducible script that:
   - hits the same model variant on three endpoints: Redwood Hosted (eu-west-1), AWS Bedrock (eu-west-1), GCP Vertex (europe-west1)
   - measures p50/p95/p99 for cold vs warm KV cache (include warm path after 500 requests)
   - collects detailed token-level timing (first token arrival + last token completion)

2) Residency/KMS note: Aisha asked specifically where the KMS keys for EU endpoints live. Please draft a one-page confirmation that covers: key region, key management (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed), and where audit logs are stored. Attach to the test run report.

3) Cost delta estimate: quick back-of-envelope comparing Redwood hosted (with batching) vs Bedrock sustained at 100k tokens/day. Put assumptions clearly (avg tokens per request, batching efficiency).

I've attached a short plan (multi-region-latency-plan.md) with target time windows and required inputs. If you can sign off on the scripts and packet captures by EOD today, I'll confirm Mon morning with Acme.

Thanks — Camila

[Attachment: multi-region-latency-plan.md (md, 4KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FW: Post-demo recap: multi-region performance & hyperscaler comparison — proposed next tests

All — quick status and owners:

- Latency scripts: Aditya will run the Bedrock/Vertex/Redwood hosted comparisons and produce p50/p95/p99 CSVs plus a single consolidated CSV for the matrix. Target: run window Mon 8 Jun 08:00–10:00 PT. Aditya, please use the test IPs Tom provides if available; otherwise use Redwood EU agents and note the origin IPs.

- Residency/KMS note: I'm drafting the one-pager confirming KMS location and log retention. Preliminary: EU endpoints use customer-region KMS keys when customers supply CMKs; Redwood-managed keys are hosted in eu-west-1 KMS and audit logs are retained in EU S3 with access logs available on request. I'll attach the note to the report.

- Cost delta: I'll run a quick cost model after the p50 numbers are in; initial estimate suggests Redwood hosted with batching should be ~15–30% lower than Bedrock for this workload due to our continuous batching + KV cache (we'll provide assumptions).

Next steps I propose:
1) Execute tests Mon 08:00 PT — Aditya to post raw results to the Drive folder and ping this thread.
2) Deliverables by Tue EOD PT: consolidated matrix (xlsx), one-page KMS/residency note (pdf), and a recommended deployment mode per region (hosted/dedicated/private).
3) If results meet Acme's p99 target, we'll propose a short pilot proposal (2-week dedicated pool in eu-west-1) and an indicative price.

Aditya / Camila: anything to add?

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
